deployment_tells: Library, not a service. Surfaces as a Python import in agent code.
Examples/ directory shows wrapper pattern: scan(user_input) -> ScanResult before LLM call.
PromptGuard-2 model weights downloaded from HF on first run; outbound HF call is the deployment fingerprint.
Operators sometimes wrap LlamaFirewall in a FastAPI/Flask service to expose REST. That deployment is the network-surface variant.
misconfig_patterns: AlignmentCheck depends on an LLM call to a configured provider; provider creds leaked in env/.env
Operators expose LlamaFirewall via a thin FastAPI wrapper without auth (default-no-auth wrapper class)
CodeShield disabled or in observe-only mode in production (config: scanner_mode=observe)

cve_catalog_2026_06_07.note: Framework is a year old (arxiv May 2025). No published CVEs. Threat model carried by the paper, not by disclosed bugs.

dork_population_substitution_risk: HIGH. Any dork that matches 'llamafirewall' or 'PromptGuard' will select operators who chose to expose the framework via a thin wrapper -- a SELF-SELECTED subpopulation that is already more security-conscious than the general agent-runtime population. Inverse selection: the operators who quietly use LlamaFirewall as a library inside their agent will be invisible. The dork measures the wrapper deployment style, not framework adoption.
lane_d_role: In-process wrapper at the tool-call layer; the canonical OSS reference for 'lib.guard(message) before send_email()'. Email is one of many tool-calls it can wrap.
